/-!
# Erdős Problem 341

*References:*
* [erdosproblems.com/341](https://www.erdosproblems.com/341)
* [Ben Green's Open Problem 7](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.1)
* [Li26] Li, Z., *Counterexamples to Erdős Problem 341* (2026),
  https://github.com/LiAlreadyExists/Erdos-341/blob/main/paper/Erdos341.pdf
-/

@[expose] public section

open Nat Set Filter
open scoped Topology

namespace Erdos341

/--
Let $A=\{a_1 < \cdots < a_k\}$ be a finite set of integers and extend it to an infinite
sequence $\overline{A}=\{a_1 < a_2 < \cdots \}$ by defining $a_{n+1}$ for $n \geq k$ to be
the least integer exceeding $a_n$ which is not of the form $a_i + a_j$ with $i,j \leq n$.
Is it true that the sequence of differences $a_{m+1}-a_m$ is eventually periodic?

This problem is discussed under Problem 7 on Green's open problems list.

The answer is no: Li [Li26] (with GPT-5.6 Sol) showed that the greedy extension of the seed set
$A = \{1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 13, 22, 27, 28, 32, 36, 40, 47, 48, 52, 63, 71, 77, 81, 89, 97\}$ has a
sequence of differences that is not eventually periodic. The linked formal proof
exhibits such a sequence `a : ℕ → ℕ` (strictly increasing, with the greedy rule holding from
some index on, and with `n ↦ a (n + 1) - a n` not eventually periodic); casting it to `ℤ`
gives a counterexample to the statement below.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos341.lean#L12"]
theorem erdos_341 :
    answer(False) ↔
      ∀ (a : ℕ → ℤ),
        (∀ᶠ n in atTop,
          IsLeast { x | a n < x ∧ x ∉ { a i + a j | (i ≤ n) (j ≤ n) } } (a (n + 1))) →
        let d := fun i ↦ a (i + 1) - a i
        ∃ p > 0, ∀ᶠ m in atTop, d (m + p) = d m := by
  sorry

end Erdos341

reformulations.difference: The source (erdosproblems.com/341, current wording) takes a nonempty finite set A = {a_1 < ⋯ < a_k} of POSITIVE integers and extends it greedily for n ≥ k. The Lean right-hand side instead ranges over every `a : ℕ → ℤ` that satisfies `IsLeast {x | a n < x ∧ x ∉ {a i + a j | (i ≤ n) (j ≤ n)}} (a (n + 1))` for all sufficiently large n. Its initial segment is arbitrary: unsorted, possibly zero or negative, possibly with repeated values, and the greedy rule may start from a term that is not the maximum. The docstring says "a finite set of integers". That was the erdosproblems.com wording before its 20 Jan 2026 revision inserted "positive"; Green's Problem 7 likewise speaks of seed "values" with no positivity condition.
reformulations.equivalence_argument:
(⇐) Every source sequence, 0-indexed, is an instance of the Lean hypothesis: it is greedy for n ≥ k−1. So the Lean universal implies the source universal.

(⇒) Let a be greedy for n ≥ N. Then a is strictly increasing from N. Choose M ≥ N with a(M) > 0 and a(M) > a(i) for all i ≤ N. For every m ≥ M, a(m) = max{a(0),…,a(m)}. Hence any sum a(i)+a(j) (i, j ≤ m) with a non-positive summand is ≤ a(m). So above a(m), the sumset of a(0..m) equals the sumset of its positive values. It follows that the tail a(M), a(M+1), … is exactly the source's greedy extension of the positive seed A = {a(i) : i ≤ M, a(i) > 0}, whose maximum is a(M). Eventual periodicity of the gaps is a tail property and survives the index shift.

Proved in Lean in /workspace/review/equiv.lean as `Review.FC_iff_Src : FC ↔ Src`, with axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only.
- `FC` is checked by `example : type_of% Erdos341.erdos_341 = (False ↔ FC) := rfl` to be the literal right-hand side.
- `Src` encodes the source literally: A : Finset ℤ, all elements positive, A nonempty; a lists A increasingly via `orderEmbOfFin`, then satisfies the greedy rule for all n ≥ A.card − 1.
- The proof constructs the positive seed and the shifted sequence explicitly and does not use the counterexample.

review.notes:
No findings. The file has a single declaration, `Erdos341.erdos_341`. It elaborates to `False ↔ ∀ a : ℕ → ℤ, (∀ᶠ n in atTop, IsLeast {x : ℤ | a n < x ∧ x ∉ {x | ∃ i ≤ n, ∃ j ≤ n, a i + a j = x}} (a (n+1))) → ∃ p : ℕ, p > 0 ∧ ∀ᶠ m in atTop, d (m+p) = d m`, with d i = a (i+1) − a i.

Checks against the source:
- The greedy rule matches Dickson's rule as stated on erdosproblems.com, in Green's Problem 7 comments and in Li's paper: least integer above a_n that is not a sum a_i + a_j with i, j ≤ n, equal summands allowed. It is not Queneau's i < j variant, which is a different problem.
- The hypothesis can be satisfied (e.g. the odd numbers) and is not vacuous.
- `answer(False)` has the right polarity for \"Is it true that … eventually periodic?\"; Li answers no.
- The broader Lean hypothesis class (any integer prefix, rule only eventually) is proved equivalent to the literal source in /workspace/review/equiv.lean; see the reformulation entry.

Checks of the fixed answer:
- The linked plby development compiles here with standard axioms only, and the exact FC statement follows from it (/workspace/review/plby_all.lean, theorem `ReviewCheck.fc_from_plby`).
- The docstring's description of the formal proof is accurate: an ℕ-valued, strictly increasing sequence, greedy from some index on, with non-eventually-periodic gaps, cast to ℤ.
- The `#L12` anchor points at `theorem not_erdos_341`.
- As an independent numerical check (/workspace/review/greedy.c), the greedy extension of Li's 21-element seed equals Li's set S on [1, 300000], and no gap period p ≤ 9187 fits the second half of the gaps.

Minor observations, not defects:
- The theorem docstring says \"a finite set of integers\". That copies the erdosproblems.com wording before the 20 Jan 2026 revision, which inserted \"positive\" (visible in the page history). It is mathematically immaterial by the equivalence above, and consistent with Green's \"seed values\". Maintainers may want to re-sync the wording.
- The file says `research solved` while erdosproblems.com still says OPEN, with Li's proof claim unreviewed there. The file's status is justified by the verified formal proof under CONTRIBUTING's criteria; it is recorded as a low-confidence status note only.

I did not consult the original Erdős–Graham (1980) text. The erdosproblems.com statement, Green's list and Li's paper agree on the formulation.
